neighbours.label: 'one' (and the verb right after it) when it picks out one member of a pair or set that is being contrasted with another member (one ... the other)
fire: The two brothers share a room, but one is neat and the other is messy.
We tested two batteries, and one lasted twice as long as the other.
There were two doors at the end of the hall; one led outside and the other to the cellar.
The cups came in two colours, one red and one blue.
Of the two bridges in town, one is much older than the other.
The sisters both play music, but one prefers piano and the other violin.
She planted two trees last spring, and one has grown faster than the other.
The farm has two dogs; one guards the sheep and the other sleeps all day.
quiet: The two brothers share a room on the top floor of the house.
We tested the battery, and it lasted for one full day.
There was only one door at the end of the hall.
The cups came in a box with one saucer missing.
The bridge in town opened at one in the afternoon.
One of the sisters' favourite songs is an old folk tune.
She planted one tree last spring near the garden gate.
The farm has a dog that guards the sheep all day.
